messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: p95/p99-latency-regression detector fired for streaming region eu-central-1. p95=850ms (threshold 400ms), p99=2.4s (threshold 1.2s) over 4m window. Auto-pager to oncall: leo, infra-oncall. https://console.redwood/dashboards/latency/eu-central-1 :rotating_light:

leo: Oncall here. Pulling up dashboards and traces now. Any recent deploys?

sofia: Checking deploy bot 527: no model or infra deploys in last 25m. But I see a spike in JS SDK reconnects and many sessions reporting stalled chunks.

rachel: Synthetic probes show increased connect time and then long idle gaps in streaming responses. Traces indicate some requests waiting on kv-lookup for 150-300ms more than baseline.

ben: I ran a quick grep on logs around 3300005800:
```
kv-cache eu-central-1 WARN key_evicted prefix=streaming:user:ctx rate=0.33
kv-cache eu-central-1 ERROR redis_read timeout=1.0s conn=42
stream-worker WARN processing_delay queue=streaming-queue size=420
```
Feels like cache churn causing worker backpressure.

leo: running quick checks:
```
# check streaming pods
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l role=stream-worker -o wide
# hpa
kubectl -n redwood get hpa streaming -o yaml
# kv pool
curl -s "https://metrics.redwood.internal/kv?region=eu-central-1&metric=pool_size"
```

infra-oncall: HPA desired=50 current=50, but scaling stalled due to node provisioning delay, cloud provider quota for GPU immediate allocation failing. There are 3 large training jobs eating up spare nodes in eu-central-1.

sofia: I can confirm eviction rate jumped exactly when a batch import job wrote many ephemeral session keys with low TTLs. Likely the import job collided with streaming key namespace.

leo: mitigation options?

rachel: Options: 1) temporary prefix-based KV isolation (deny import job access to streaming prefix), 2) route streaming traffic to warm fallback region (eu-west-2) for affected customers, 3) throttle the bulk import job and evict TTL churn, 4) flip streaming routes to model-compact which reduces KV lookups because of smaller contexts.

ben: Quick, low-risk step: pause the import job and throttle it to 10% until KV eviction subsides. I can do that now.

ops-bot: ACTION REQUEST: pause-job import-bulk-2026 triggered by ben at 3300005841. Please ack.

leo: ack. ben, pause it and confirm.

ben: paused import-bulk-2026. Eviction rate dropped from 0.33 -> 0.12 within 60s. p95 fell to ~420ms but p99 still around 1.3s.

leo: good. Next, I'll route ~20% of streaming-prod-euc to eu-west-2 to reduce load and buy time for KV heal. Running routing change.

leo: command:
```
redwoodctl routing adjust --from streaming-prod-euc --to streaming-prod-euw --percent 20 --reason "latency mitigation"
```

ops-bot: ROUTE CHANGE: streaming-prod-euc -> streaming-prod-euw 20% applied by leo at 3300005890. Change ID rc_91a2.

sofia: After route shift, p95 steady ~380ms, p99 at ~980ms. Backpressure on workers decreased (queue size down to ~180).

infra-oncall: I asked infra to preempt non-critical training jobs and requested emergency quota increase. Provider acked request pending manual approval; expected ~12-18m.

rachel: Customer impact: monitored customers with long-context sessions in eu-central-1 showed reconnect spikes and partial stalls for ~6 minutes before mitigations. No data corruption, just latency/connectivity pain. I'll prepare outreach note.

leo: marking incident as "partial mitigation". We'll keep live watch for 30m and coordinate post-incident tasks. If p99 > 1.5s again we escalate to on-call manager.

ben: follow-up runbook items (short):
- audit import job key prefixes and fix TTL policy (assign longer TTL or separate namespace)
- add HPA tweak to prefer scale-up when kv.latency > 200ms
- add temporary rate-limit on long context connections during region anomalies
- add alert for eviction_rate > 0.2 to trigger import job pause automation

ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: owner=leo, severity=sev2, state=monitoring. Postmortem owner rachel. :spiral_calendar:

sofia: I'll also schedule a quick hotfix to avoid future namespace collisions: import jobs default prefix changed to import:bulk: and we enforce a 5s min TTL.

leo: thanks team. Keeping thread pinned. Will update status page and customer comms. If any regressions hit p99 thresholds, reopen page immediately. :thumbsup:
summary: Realtime p95/p99 detector alerted for eu-central-1; root cause was TTL churn from a bulk import job causing KV eviction and streaming worker backpressure; mitigations: paused import job, routed 20% traffic to fallback region, requested quota bump, assigned postmortem to rachel
